issues.display_title: Issue #353: Dashboard: ownership filter for the project list (My projects / Shared with me)
issues.main_description_html:
Design task for #349 — [PRD] Update Collaborators, Roles, and Permissions (R17, §B1).

RESULT

Branch: design/collaborators-roles-and-permissions

Ownership filter added to the dashboard toolbar and wired through the existing list pipeline.

What landed:

  • OwnershipMenu.tsx (new) — Popover-based filter built on the same control as SortMenu and placed beside it. Trigger states the current choice; options are a radiogroup so the selection is announced without colour.
  • lib/dashboard/projects.ts — OWNERSHIP_OPTIONS, isOwnedByMe(), filterByOwnership() and ownershipEmptyCopy(). Ownership prefers the server's is_owner, falls back to a case-insensitive owner_email match, and treats an unknown project as owned rather than stripping the owner of their own controls.
  • useDashboard.ts / dashboard/page.tsx — ownership held as list state and applied over the loaded projects; no refetch on filter change.
  • DashboardStates.tsx — empty state takes the filter-aware copy so it names what was filtered.

Seam left for the functional pack: owner_email is not on the list payload yet, so a project owned by someone else has no address to show — noted as TODO(backend) at the single point that reads it. Filling it must not cost a request per row.

Files: src/app/dashboard/OwnershipMenu.tsx, src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts, src/app/dashboard/page.tsx, src/lib/dashboard/projects.ts, src/components/dashboard/DashboardStates.tsx, src/lib/collaboration/types.ts

issues.display_title: Issue #354: Dashboard: update project list layout with the Owner value
issues.main_description_html:
Design task for #349 — [PRD] Update Collaborators, Roles, and Permissions (R16, §B1).

Scope

Update the dashboard project list layout so ownership is visible on every project, and so owner-only actions explain themselves instead of failing late.

  • Owner value on each project: Me for your own, the owner's email address otherwise
  • Consistent across the Recent tiles, the grid cards and the list rows
  • Publish / unpublish / delete stay visible for non-owners but open an explanatory dialog naming the owner, rather than a destructive confirm that 403s

Acceptance criteria

  • Every project surface shows an owner value; long addresses truncate without breaking layout
  • Owner reads "Me" for your own projects
  • Publish / unpublish / delete on someone else's project open the owner-only dialog, never the confirm
  • The message names who can help — no "forbidden" or "unauthorised" wording
  • Owner value is plain text, not colour-coded

RESULT

Branch: design/collaborators-roles-and-permissions

Owner surfaced across all three project layouts, and the non-owner path rerouted to a shared explanatory dialog.

What landed:

  • ProjectViews.tsx — new OwnerValue cell (person icon + label) added to the Recent tile, grid card and list row. Truncates with a title so a long address can't break the layout; plain text, never colour-coded.
  • lib/dashboard/projects.ts — ownerLabel() returns "Me" for your own projects, the owner's email otherwise, and null when ownership is genuinely unknown so the column can say so instead of inventing a name.
  • OwnerOnlyDialog.tsx (new, shared) replaces the local NotOwnerDialog: one dialog for publish / unpublish / delete, taking the owner's email and naming them in the message. The OwnerOnlyAction type moved out of ProjectViews so Preview reuses the same one.
  • Owner-only actions stay visible rather than disappearing (§A9) — the collaborator sees why, and never reaches the destructive confirm.

Seam left for the functional pack: owner_email is absent from the list payload, so the dialog falls back to the collaboration mock address; marked TODO(backend) where it is read.

Files: src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx, src/components/collaboration/OwnerOnlyDialog.tsx, src/components/preview/PreviewConfirmDialog.tsx, src/lib/dashboard/projects.ts

issues.display_title: Issue #355: Editor: rename Share to Collab and open Manage Collaborators
issues.main_description_html:
Design task for #349 — [PRD] Update Collaborators, Roles, and Permissions (R5, §B2).

RESULT

Branch: design/collaborators-roles-and-permissions

Share replaced by Collab, and the inline panel replaced by a real modal.

What landed:

  • EditorTopbar.tsx — button relabelled Collab with the Users icon (was Share2), now opening ManageCollaboratorsDialog. Save status is swapped for the "Viewing only" label in a Viewer's top bar; theme, Collab and Preview stay in every role. Import / Export are removed from the project menu for a Viewer only — the one thing that menu changes by role.
  • ShareMembersPanel.tsx deleted (−149 lines). Its member management was not lost: the new ManageCollaboratorsDialog container assembles the same listMembers / inviteMember / updateMemberRole / removeMember server actions behind the redesigned modal.
  • ManageCollaboratorsDialog.tsx (new) — the data container; the modal itself stays presentational.
  • Role reads through a single seam (useDesignRole) so the functional pack swaps one call, not forty call sites.

Files: src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx, src/components/editor/collab/ManageCollaboratorsDialog.tsx, src/components/editor/collab/ShareMembersPanel.tsx (deleted)

issues.display_title: Issue #356: Editor: update the Manage Collaborators modal (roles, invite, owner-only controls)
issues.main_description_html:
Design task for #349 — [PRD] Update Collaborators, Roles, and Permissions (R4, R6, R7, R11 · §B3–§B5).

RESULT

Branch: design/collaborators-roles-and-permissions

Manage Collaborators built as one modal serving all three roles.

What landed:

  • ManageCollaboratorsModal.tsx — the modal. canManage is the whole role difference: true gives role dropdowns, remove buttons and the invite section; false gives the same title and list with roles as static text and nothing to act on. Owner sorts first, then everyone by name falling back to email. The list area scrolls; the invite section stays put beneath it. Built on PreviewModal, so it traps focus, labels itself from the title, closes on Escape and backdrop, and returns focus to Collab. Shell renders immediately and the list skeletons while loading.
  • CollaboratorRow.tsx — avatar with initials fallback, name promoting to email when absent, "You" marker on your own row, quiet "Invited" chip, and a locked owner row. Plus CollaboratorRowSkeleton.
  • InviteCollaboratorForm.tsx — email + role dropdown defaulting to Viewer, with the join-invite offer for unregistered addresses.
  • lib/collaboration/invite.ts — the invite flow as an explicit state machine (idle · checking · added · not-registered · join-invite-sending · join-invite-sent · already-member · failed), so the outcomes live in one place instead of scattered booleans. Copy is plain language throughout.
  • lib/collaboration/collaborators.ts, types.ts — view-model shapes and ordering; nothing in the presentational layer resolves a role or calls an endpoint.
  • ManageCollaboratorsDialog.tsx — container wiring the modal to the existing member server actions, with ActionToastRegion for outcomes.

Seam left for the functional pack: Member carries only { user_id, email, name, role } — avatars and invitation status have no source yet, so no avatar renders (initials fallback) and the Invited chip stays unused; marked TODO(backend).

Files: src/components/collaboration/ManageCollaboratorsModal.tsx, CollaboratorRow.tsx, InviteCollaboratorForm.tsx, src/lib/collaboration/invite.ts, collaborators.ts, types.ts, src/components/editor/collab/ManageCollaboratorsDialog.tsx, src/components/ui/action-toast.tsx

issues.display_title: Issue #357: Editor and Preview: read-only layouts for the Viewer role
issues.main_description_html:
Design task for #349 — [PRD] Update Collaborators, Roles, and Permissions (R14 · §A1, §A2, §B6–§B9).

RESULT

Branch: design/collaborators-roles-and-permissions

Viewer read-only layouts built for both the Editor and Preview, on a single capability model.

Permission model:

  • lib/collaboration/capabilities.ts — one place deriving canEdit / canManageAccess / canDecideFate / canImportExport. Components read capabilities, never roles, so a new role or a nuance like "editors can't export" changes one line instead of forty call sites. resolveRole() resolves owner → known role → viewer, never owner by default: guessing high is the one direction that hands out access nobody granted.
  • useProjectCapabilities.ts, ownerGuard.ts — the hook seam and the owner-only guard.
  • ViewingOnlyBadge.tsx — the shared label, announced rather than colour-only.

Editor (project mode + map mode):

  • Top bar shows "Viewing only" in place of the save status; Import / Export removed from the project menu.
  • Editing removed — not disabled — across EditorPanel, EditorBottomToolbar, SelectionToolbar, SelectionToolbars (map mode), SelectedFeaturePanel, InformationSection, InformationListSection, ObjectSection, FloorplanEditor and EmptyProjectPlaceholder.
  • Theme, Collab and Preview stay in every role; an Editor's editor is identical to an Owner's apart from owner-only controls.

Preview:

  • PreviewTopbar — Viewer sees status + "Viewing only" + theme, plus the live link and share once published, and nothing else. Publish / unpublish route through the shared OwnerOnlyDialog, which names the owner. Toasts moved onto the shared ActionToastRegion.

Review harness: /design-preview/collaboration renders every role state side by side against seeded data — design-only route, not a production surface.

Seams left for the functional pack: the REST project payload carries no role field, so role resolves via the collab socket session and falls back to Viewer until it arrives; owner_email is likewise absent and falls back to the mock. Both are marked TODO(backend) at the single point each is read.
